learning_outcomes.text: Students who have successfully studied this module have a broad knowledge of basic radio technologies and systems.

Students who have successfully studied this module have detailed knowledge in the areas of wave propagation and electromagnetic fields, radio channel, antennas, radio network planning, access methods (duplex, multiplex) as well as the architecture of various radio systems (WLAN, mobile radio, broadcast radio, satellite radio).

Students who have successfully studied this module have practical knowledge in the planning of radio systems and can apply their acquired knowledge in practice to assess and design radio systems. They can quantitatively examine the behavior of high-frequency circuits in the time domain (oscilloscope) and in the frequency domain (spectral analyzer, network analyzer).
Students master the technologies of radio systems and can use them purposefully to solve similar new problems.
Students who have successfully studied this module can assess the performance of various radio technologies and develop innovative solutions for new problems.

Students who have successfully studied this module master the terminology of radio networks and high-frequency technology. They can understand technical articles, classify technologies, and analyze and measure radio networks in a team.

Students who have successfully studied this module can apply their acquired knowledge of radio technologies in practice for planning, development, and performance evaluation. They can select, configure, integrate, and measure suitable components for the construction of radio systems.

syllabus_topics: Measurement and analysis of high-frequency signals (theory of electrical lines, Smith chart, scattering parameters)
Multiplex and duplex procedures; spread spectrum procedures
Radio systems (local radio systems, broadcasting, mobile radio, satellite radio)
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is either an oral examination or a written exam. The duration of the oral examination is specified in the general part of the examination regulations. The scope of the written exam is specified in the valid study regulations. An ungraded experimental work consisting of approximately 6 experiments is also required.
